title: Northbridge KPI Odyssey — daily scratch
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight personal scratch for tracking a 3-week micro-OKR I want to trial — called the "Northbridge" experiment. Intention: keep a tight loop (daily micro-check, weekly reflection) focused on a small set of measurable behaviours and output. Not a team doc — for my use, but sometimes shareable as a snapshot at end of week.

Why this feels different:
- Too many long-term goals get fuzzy; I want a 21-day test that treats metrics as learning signals rather than targets.
- Emphasis on energy budget and elapsed attention (not just deliverables).
- Mix quantitative (numbers I can measure) and qualitative (mood/notes).

Micro-OKR summary (21 days):
- Objective: Shrink friction for small evals and get 3 reliable results I can act on.
- Key Result 1 (KR1): Run 12 quick eval runs (<= 1 hour each) and capture structured notes.
- Key Result 2 (KR2): Improve local day-to-day throughput metric — median time from hypothesis->first-result from 4d -> <= 36h for 60% of runs.
- Key Result 3 (KR3): Ship 1 small improvement (doc + script) that saves at least 10m per run for the team.

Daily ritual (5 mins in morning, 10 mins before EOD):
- Morning: 1-line intent (what I’ll attempt today in 2–3 bullets); energy budget (hours avail); blockers to clear.
- EOD: quick tally — runs started, runs completed, median turnaround for runs, notes link, mood (1-5).

Template — copy for each day:
- Date: 2025-08-__
- Intent: 
  - Experiment(s): e.g., small-quant-compare on q4-bert variant
  - Time budget: 3h (blocks: 9–11am)
  - Expected output: 1 draft report + 3 eval snapshots
- Runs: started X / completed Y 
- Turnaround times (in hours): [list] 
- Obvious friction: (tools/infra/ops)
- Mood / energy: 4/5
- Quick note: "what I learned" (1–2 lines)
- Blockers to escalate: (JIRA keys, Slack threads)

Weekly check (every Mon morning for previous week):
- Week window: Mon–Sun
- KR progress update:
  - KR1: 5/12 runs completed (on track / behind)
  - KR2: median H->R: 52h (baseline 96h) -> trend: improving
  - KR3: patch idea: add small caching hook (proto) -> estimate savings 12m/run
- Top wins this week:
  - Removed a 30m manual step in data prep using quick script (link to gist)
  - Found a reproducibility flake — opened JIRA RI-1293
- Top learnings / pivots:
  - Several runs were blocked by env drift; allocate 1h this week to a reproducible env checklist
- Shareable snapshot for team (1–2 lines): "Ran 5 micro-evals; found env drift as primary throughput bottleneck; prototyping local cache to save ~12m/run."

Unresolved questions / hypotheses:
- H1: If I invest 2h up-front in templated eval scripts, I can reduce median H->R by >25% for repeat runs.
- H2: The largest variance comes from data copying; caching will have diminishing returns after first 8 runs.
- H3: Blocking on infra (quota/VM spin) correlates with time-of-day; schedule heavy runs after 10pm? (observe)

Action backlog (ordered):
- [ ] Create env-checklist + runbook (target: 2025-08-20) — high priority
- [ ] Prototype cache wrapper + measure savings (target: 2025-08-22) — medium
- [ ] Convert 3 most-common eval steps into script templates (target: 2025-08-24) — medium
- [ ] Share weekly snapshot with Ariane & Noah for feedback (target: Monday standup) — low

Mini-retro (end of 21 days):
- What worked: short daily rituals keep momentum; counting runs helps motivation; quick scripts paid back time fast.
- What didn’t: I still under-estimated time for reproducibility fixes; cross-team dependencies matter more than I thought.
- New baseline: if I can get H->R median to 36h, I’ll adopt the process as "small-eval standard" for my team.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep daily entries terse; use bullet lines only — saves cognitive load when reviewing.
- Link every run to a small note file (date + descriptor) — makes weekly aggregation trivial.
- If a blocker repeats twice, escalate with a JIRA and Slack mention — don’t keep it in private notebook.

Useful links / quick references:
- Quickbench script: github.com/redwood-inference/quickbench (PR #57)
